# test_email_validation.py

import pytest

from your_module import is_valid_email  # replace "your_module" with the actual module name


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "email",
    [
        "user@example.com",
        "USER@example.COM",
        "user.name@example.com",
        "user_name@example.com",
        "user-name@example.com",
        "user+tag@example.com",
        "user%tag@example.com",
        "u@x.io",
        "user@example.co.uk",
        "user@sub.domain.example.com",
        "user@example.museum",
        "user123@example123.com",
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_happy_path(email):
    assert is_valid_email(email) is True


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "email",
    [
        "",
        "plainaddress",
        "userexample.com",
        "@example.com",
        "user@",
        "user@com",
        "user@example",
        "user@example.c",
        "user@example.123",
        "user@example.c0m",
        "user@exa_mple.com",
        "user name@example.com",
        "user@example .com",
        "user@ example.com",
        "user@@example.com",
        "user@example@com",
        " user@example.com",
        "user@example.com ",
        "user@example,com",
        "user#example.com",
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_invalid_formats(email):
    assert is_valid_email(email) is False


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "email",
    [
        None,
        123,
        12.34,
        [],
        {},
        b"user@example.com",
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_non_string_inputs_raise_type_error(email):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        is_valid_email(email)


@pytest.mark.xfail(

    reason="Current implementation uses re.match with $, which accepts a trailing newline.",
)
def test_is_valid_email_rejects_trailing_newline():
    assert is_valid_email("user@example.com\n") is False
